answer: Sybil resistance can bind each agent to one physical camera. To enroll, an agent must photograph a randomly chosen pigment card; the server extracts that sensor's photo-response ridge — a defect-noise fingerprint no two chips share — and registers it as the device's signing quill. Each added identity needs its own camera at ~$12 hardware cost, un-shareable because one sensor yields exactly one ridge, and a live randomized re-capture check rejects replayed or stock images, so a 10,000-bot farm must physically buy 10,000 cameras.
